h1: The 7 Best 8-Port Network Switches for Home and Small Office, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 eight-port network switches, unmanaged, smart managed and 2.5G, compared on VLANs, warranty, speed and fanless design.
summary: The NETGEAR GS308E Easy Smart Managed Switch is the best 8-port switch for most people, a gigabit box with up to 64 VLANs for under $25. The TP-Link TL-SG108E is the runner-up with link aggregation and a 3-year warranty, the Aruba Instant On 1830 is the best app-managed choice, and the TP-Link TL-SG108S-M2 is the pick for 2.5G speeds.
intro: The 8-port switch is the most over-bought box in networking. People pay for management features they never open, or skip them and later wish they had a way to separate a camera network from the family laptop. The honest question is whether you will ever use a VLAN, a port mirror or a link aggregation group. If the answer is no, an unmanaged switch is all you need; if maybe, a smart switch costs almost nothing extra.

This ranking sorts seven 8-port switches by management features, port speed, warranty and power options. We read the product titles and specification lists supplied, and price shows as buckets only. A smart managed switch is configured through a web page, not a command line, so it suits home users who want a bit more control without learning a new operating system.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308E 8-Port Easy Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: An 8-port smart switch with up to 64 VLANs, a cross-platform web interface and automatic protection, for under $25.
products.description:
The GS308E offers eight ports, up to 64 VLANs, a cross-platform web interface and automatic DoS, loop and storm protection. Pricing lands under $25.

It wins because it delivers smart features at an unmanaged price. VLANs let you separate cameras, guests and work devices on one box, and loop protection saves you from the classic mistake of plugging a cable into two ports on the same switch. A web interface that works on any platform means no special software. It is the most capable of the cheap models.

Buy it if you want a bit of control for almost nothing. Skip it if you want plug-and-forget with no interface.
products.idealFor: Homes wanting VLANs on a budget.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG108E 8-Port Easy Smart Switch
products.verdict: A smart 8-port switch with 32 VLANs, link aggregation and a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
The TL-SG108E is an 8-port easy smart switch with up to 32 simultaneous VLANs, link aggregation and a 3-year warranty. Pricing lands under $25.

It ranks second because link aggregation lets you combine ports for a faster link to a NAS or server, and the 3-year warranty is longer than most budget switches. Thirty-two VLANs are enough for home use. It loses to the NETGEAR on VLAN count and automatic protection features.

Choose it for LAG and a longer warranty. Skip it if you want the most VLANs.
products.idealFor: Users who want LAG and a long warranty.

products.name: Aruba Instant On 1830 8G Smart Switch
products.verdict: A fanless 8-port smart switch with app and web management that can be powered by upstream PoE.
products.description:
The Aruba Instant On 1830 8G has eight gigabit ports, a fanless design, app and web management, and can be powered via upstream PoE. Pricing is $100 to $200.

It ranks third because the management tools are more polished than the budget models, and powering it from a PoE port upstream can simplify installs in awkward spots. It costs several times more than the NETGEAR and TP-Link smart switches, which makes it hard to justify unless you value the app.

Pick it for a tidy, managed small-office setup. Skip it if you are on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG108S-M2 8-Port 2.5G Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Eight 2.5G ports with 40Gbps capacity that run over existing Cat5e, fanless and unmanaged.
products.description:
The TL-SG108S-M2 has eight 2.5G ports, 40Gbps switching capacity, runs over existing Cat5e cabling and is fanless and unmanaged. Pricing is $50 to $100.

It ranks fourth because 2.5G is the upgrade path for fast broadband and NAS use, and it works on the cable already in your walls. For a home with a 2.5G modem or a computer with a 2.5G port, it removes a bottleneck. It is unmanaged, so it offers no VLANs.

Choose it if you have 2.5G devices. Skip it if everything on your network is gigabit.
products.idealFor: Homes with 2.5G devices or a fast NAS.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG108 8-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: An 8-port gigabit unmanaged switch in a shielded metal housing with 24x7 support.
products.description:
The TL-SG108 has eight gigabit ports in a shielded metal housing, fanless, plug-and-play, with 24x7 live technical support. Pricing lands under $25.

It ranks fifth because it is the simplest: plug cables in and it works. A metal housing resists interference and dissipates heat for a fanless box, and live support is rare at this price. It lacks VLANs, which the E models include at the same price.

Buy it for a no-fuss desk switch. Skip it if you might want VLANs.
products.idealFor: A simple desk or TV switch.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308 8-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: A fanless unmanaged gigabit switch with 802.3az energy-efficient Ethernet and a metal housing.
products.description:
The NETGEAR GS308 has eight gigabit ports, a fanless metal housing, 802.3az power saving on idle ports plus a bracket-free wall or desk placement. Pricing lands under $25.

It ranks sixth because it is a sound unmanaged switch with energy saving, but the smart GS308E costs the same and does more. Energy-efficient Ethernet reduces power on idle ports, which is a small saving for a box left on 24 hours a day.

Choose it for a basic switch with a wall mount option. Skip it if the E model is available at the same price.
products.skipIf: You want VLANs for the same money.

products.name: NETGEAR GS108 8-Port Gigabit ProSAFE Switch
products.verdict: A fanless 8-port gigabit ProSAFE switch with desktop or wall mounting.
products.description:
The NETGEAR GS108 has eight gigabit ports, a fanless design, ProSAFE lifetime protection heritage and desktop or wall mounting. Pricing is $25 to $50.

It ranks last because it costs more than the GS308 and the TP-Link units while offering fewer features. The ProSAFE name carries a reputation for durability, and lifetime protection heritage suggests a long cover, but the listing does not spell out terms.

Buy it if you trust the ProSAFE name. Skip it if you can buy a cheaper model with more features.
products.idealFor: Buyers who trust the ProSAFE name.
products.skipIf: You want more features for less.

whatMatters.detail: An unmanaged switch works out of the box with no settings. A smart switch adds a web page for VLANs, aggregation and monitoring. At under $25 the smart models are the better buy for most.
VLANs split one switch into separate networks, which keeps cameras, guests and work devices apart. Home users rarely need more than a few. Check the stated VLAN count.
Gigabit is plenty for most homes. 2.5G helps with fast internet and NAS use and runs on Cat5e cable. Check that your devices have matching ports before you pay for 2.5G.
Fanless switches are silent and have no moving parts to fail. At eight ports they run cool enough to sit on a desk. Look for fanless in the listing.
Most switches use a wall adapter. The Aruba can be powered from an upstream PoE port, which helps in ceiling or wall installs. Note that none of these supply PoE to other devices.

faq.q: Do I need a managed switch at home?
faq.a: Not usually, but a smart switch costs about the same as an unmanaged one and gives you VLANs and monitoring if you want them later.
Looping two ports of the same switch together. This floods the network. Switches with loop protection, like the GS308E, handle it.

faq.q: Is the 2.5G switch worth it over gigabit?
faq.a: Only if you have 2.5G devices. Otherwise you pay for speed you cannot use.
Unmanaged switches need nothing but power and cables. Smart switches add a web page for settings, which takes a few minutes.

faq.q: How do I look after a switch?
faq.a: Keep vents clear, avoid stacking heavy items on top and update firmware on managed models.
No. These listings are for non-PoE switches. The Aruba can be powered by an upstream PoE port, but it does not supply PoE.

finalTake: The NETGEAR GS308E is the best 8-port network switch for most people, with up to 64 VLANs, loop protection and a very low price. The TP-Link TL-SG108E is the pick for link aggregation and a 3-year warranty, the Aruba Instant On 1830 suits app-managed small offices, and the TL-SG108S-M2 is the 2.5G upgrade. Buy smart over unmanaged when prices are equal.
